name: env-key-replacer-nested-keys
description: Tests SetEnvKeyReplacer for nested keys with dots mapping to underscore env vars
prompt: I'm using viper in my Go service. I have a config key 'database.host' that should be configurable via an env var. I've set AutomaticEnv() and SetEnvPrefix('APP'). My env var APP_DATABASE_HOST is set but viper returns the default. What's wrong?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest checking the env var name, case sensitivity, or re-reading the config. The root cause is the missing SetEnvKeyReplacer — viper looks for APP_DATABASE.HOST (dot preserved), not APP_DATABASE_HOST.

assertions.text: Identifies the root cause as missing SetEnvKeyReplacer
Explains that viper preserves the dot in 'database.host' when looking up the env var
Provides the fix: viper.SetEnvKeyReplacer(strings.NewReplacer(".", "_"))
Shows that the full setup requires prefix + replacer + AutomaticEnv together
Does NOT suggest renaming the config key to avoid dots

name: sub-returns-nil
description: Tests that viper.Sub() returns nil when the key doesn't exist and must be nil-checked
prompt: I'm using viper.Sub('database') in my Go service to get a sub-viper for database config, then calling sub.Unmarshal(&dbCfg). Occasionally the service panics with a nil pointer dereference. What's happening?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest checking the config file format or adding error handling to Unmarshal. The root cause is Sub() returning nil when the 'database' key doesn't exist, and nil.Unmarshal panics.

assertions.text: Identifies that viper.Sub() returns nil when the key doesn't exist
Shows adding a nil check: if sub := viper.Sub("database"); sub != nil { ... }
Suggests returning a clear error or using defaults when sub is nil
Does NOT suggest checking err from Sub() (it returns no error, only nil)
Optionally suggests UnmarshalKey("database", &dbCfg) as an alternative that avoids Sub() entirely

name: config-file-not-found-graceful
description: Tests graceful handling of ConfigFileNotFoundError for optional config files
prompt: My Go service uses viper to read a config file. When users run it without a config file, it crashes with 'Config File config not found in ...'. The config file should be optional. How do I fix this?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest pre-checking if the file exists before calling ReadInConfig, or using os.Stat. The correct pattern is errors.As with viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError.

assertions.text: Detects the missing file with errors.As against a value-typed target (var notFound viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError) or an equivalent type assertion (err.(viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError)) — a *viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError pointer target never matches, because viper returns the error by value
Only propagates errors that are NOT ConfigFileNotFoundError
Continues execution normally when the config file is not found
Does NOT use os.Stat or file existence check as the solution
Does NOT ignore all errors from ReadInConfig (real errors like bad YAML should still propagate)

name: global-viper-test-pollution
description: Tests viper.New() for test isolation instead of the global instance
prompt: My Go tests for config loading are flaky — they pass when run in isolation but fail in a certain order. Each test calls viper.SetConfigFile and viper.ReadInConfig. What's causing this and how do I fix it?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest adding t.Cleanup(viper.Reset) or running tests with -count=1. The correct fix is creating viper.New() per test to avoid shared global state.

assertions.text: Identifies the root cause as shared global viper state across tests
Recommends viper.New() per test to create an isolated instance
Shows v := viper.New() and using v.SetConfigFile, v.ReadInConfig, etc.
Does NOT recommend viper.Reset() as the primary solution
Explains why the tests are order-dependent (state set in one test persists to the next)

name: unmarshal-mapstructure-tags
description: Tests use of mapstructure struct tags for correct Unmarshal behavior
prompt: I'm unmarshaling my viper config into a Go struct. My config file has 'max_conn: 25' but after calling viper.Unmarshal(&cfg), cfg.MaxConn is always 0. My struct has field MaxConn int. What's wrong?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest checking the config file key name or viper.GetInt. The fix is adding mapstructure:"max_conn" tag — without it, mapstructure uses case-insensitive name matching but doesn't handle underscores to camel-case conversion.

assertions.text: Identifies the missing mapstructure struct tag as the root cause
Shows adding `mapstructure:"max_conn"` to the MaxConn field
Explains that mapstructure does case-insensitive matching but not underscore-to-camelcase conversion
Does NOT suggest using viper.GetInt as the fix (Unmarshal should work once tagged correctly)

name: bind-pflag-timing
description: Tests that a flag binding must exist before the first read of its key, such as a viper.Unmarshal in the root's PersistentPreRunE
prompt: I'm integrating cobra and viper in my Go CLI. The root command's PersistentPreRunE calls viper.Unmarshal(&cfg) into a package-level Config struct. My serve command defines a --port flag and calls viper.BindPFlag("port", cmd.Flags().Lookup("port")) at the start of its RunE, then starts the server on cfg.Port. The server always listens on the default 8080, even when I pass --port 9090. Why?
trap: Without the skill, the model may check the flag name spelling, or claim that cobra's flag parsing already happened so a late binding misses the flag's Changed state. Viper reads bound flags lazily at each Get or Unmarshal — the real problem is that cfg was decoded in PersistentPreRunE before RunE created the binding. The binding must move to init() or ahead of the Unmarshal.

assertions.text: Identifies that cfg was unmarshaled in PersistentPreRunE before the BindPFlag call in RunE ran, so the struct never saw the flag
Recommends moving BindPFlag to init() or PersistentPreRunE
Explains that viper reads a bound flag's value and Changed state lazily at Get/Unmarshal time, so the binding only has to exist before the first read of the key
Shows the correct pattern: define flag + BindPFlag in init()

name: viper-key-case-insensitivity
description: Tests understanding that viper keys are always lowercased internally
prompt: I'm calling viper.GetString('DATABASE_HOST') in my Go service to read a config key. The config file has 'database_host: localhost' but I get an empty string. What's wrong?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest checking env binding or config format. Viper lowercases all keys internally — 'DATABASE_HOST' is stored as 'database_host', but the lookup 'DATABASE_HOST' is also lowercased to 'database_host', so it should match. However, this highlights the convention: always use lowercase keys in viper calls.

assertions.text: Explains that viper normalizes all keys to lowercase internally
Recommends using lowercase keys consistently in viper.Get* calls
Identifies that viper.GetString("database_host") is the correct form
Notes that while viper.GetString("DATABASE_HOST") also works (due to lowercasing), using uppercase keys is a source of confusion

name: duration-decode-hook
description: Tests that a custom decode hook replaces viper's default hook chain, so time.Duration fields stop decoding unless the duration hook is composed back in
prompt: My Go viper config has 'timeout: 30s' and 'bind_addr: 10.0.0.1' in the YAML file. My struct has Timeout time.Duration and BindAddr net.IP fields with mapstructure tags, and I call viper.Unmarshal(&cfg, viper.DecodeHook(mapstructure.StringToIPHookFunc())) so the IP parses. Unmarshal fails with "'timeout' cannot parse value as 'time.Duration'" and cfg.Timeout is 0. Why?
trap: Without the skill, the model may assume mapstructure never decodes durations, or suggest GetDuration or a nanosecond config value. Viper's default decoder already includes StringToTimeDurationHookFunc (plus a comma-splitting slice hook); viper.DecodeHook(...) replaces that chain instead of appending to it, so the IP hook must be composed with the duration hook.

assertions.text: Identifies that viper.DecodeHook(...) replaces viper's default decode hook chain, which already contains the duration hook, rather than adding to it
Composes the IP hook with the duration hook via mapstructure.ComposeDecodeHookFunc — in viper.DecodeHook(...), or in a DecoderConfig option that composes with the existing dc.DecodeHook
Uses mapstructure.StringToTimeDurationHookFunc() as part of the hook
Does NOT suggest changing the config value to nanoseconds

name: watch-config-atomic-rename-trap
description: Tests that a Remove event for the config path — produced on macOS when a save renames a temp file over the config — ends viper's watch loop permanently
prompt: I've set up viper.WatchConfig() in my Go service on macOS. Hot reload works when I append to the config file with echo, but after I save the file once from my editor, the OnConfigChange callback never fires again — not even for later echo appends. What's happening?
trap: Without the skill, the model may suggest checking the fsnotify version, debugging the callback, or blame the editor replacing the watched inode. Viper watches the config file's directory; the editor's atomic save (write temp file, rename over the original) arrives on macOS as Remove then Create, and the Remove event for the config path ends viper's watch loop for good.

assertions.text: Explains that the editor saves atomically — it writes a temp file and renames it over the original
Explains that viper watches the config file's directory and that the Remove event for the config path, emitted on macOS when a file is renamed over it, ends the watch loop permanently
Recommends testing hot-reload using direct writes (os.WriteFile) rather than editor saves
Does NOT suggest switching to a different editor as the fix

name: weakly-typed-input-env-bool
description: Tests that viper.Unmarshal ignores keys that exist only as env vars under AutomaticEnv, even though viper.Get* sees them
prompt: My Go service has a Config struct with an Enabled bool field and mapstructure tag. Setting MY_APP_ENABLED=true in the environment and calling viper.Unmarshal leaves cfg.Enabled as false, even though viper.GetBool works. Why?
trap: Without the skill, the model may blame string-to-bool conversion and enable WeaklyTypedInput, which viper already enables by default. The real cause is that Unmarshal decodes only keys viper already knows (config file, SetDefault, BindEnv, bound flags); AutomaticEnv answers Get calls but registers no keys, so the env-only 'enabled' key is skipped.

assertions.text: Identifies that Unmarshal decodes only keys viper already knows (config file, SetDefault, BindEnv, bound flags) and that AutomaticEnv does not register the env-only 'enabled' key
Registers the key before Unmarshal with viper.BindEnv("enabled") or viper.SetDefault("enabled", false), or builds the instance with viper.NewWithOptions(viper.ExperimentalBindStruct())
Rules out string-to-bool conversion as the cause — viper's default decoder already decodes weakly typed input such as "true" into bool
Does NOT suggest changing the env var format or using only viper.GetBool as the fix
